import json
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Extract lists
df_spend = pd.DataFrame(data['education_spending']['data'])
df_pisa = pd.DataFrame(data['pisa_scores']['data'])
df_enroll = pd.DataFrame(data['tertiary_enrollment']['data'])
df_unemp = pd.DataFrame(data['youth_unemployment']['data'])

# Merge
df = df_spend.merge(df_pisa, on='country')
df = df.merge(df_enroll, on='country')
df = df.merge(df_unemp, on='country')

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'sans-serif'
plt.rcParams['font.sans-serif'] = ['Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans']
plt.rcParams['axes.edgecolor'] = '#333333'
plt.rcParams['axes.linewidth'] = 0.8
plt.rcParams['axes.labelcolor'] = '#333333'
plt.rcParams['xtick.color'] = '#333333'
plt.rcParams['ytick.color'] = '#333333'

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create scatter plot
# Bubble size: University enrollment rate
# Bubble color: Youth unemployment rate
scatter = ax.scatter(
    df['edu_spending_pct_gdp'], 
    df['pisa_avg'], 
    s=df['enrollment_rate'] * 8, # scale up size
    c=df['youth_unemp_rate'], 
    cmap='coolwarm', # coolwarm: low unemp is cool (blue), high unemp is warm (red)
    alpha=0.7, 
    edgecolors='white', 
    linewidth=1.5
)

# Add colorbar for youth unemployment
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax, shrink=0.7, aspect=20, pad=0.03)
cbar.set_label('Youth Unemployment Rate (%)', fontsize=11, labelpad=10, color='#333333')
cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=10, colors='#333333')
cbar.outline.set_edgecolor('none')

# Add size legend for enrollment
sizes = [40, 70, 100]
legend_elements = [plt.scatter([], [], s=size*8, c='gray', alpha=0.5, edgecolors='white', label=f'{size}%') for size in sizes]
legend = ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, title='Tertiary Enrollment\n(% of age cohort)', loc='lower right', 
                   frameon=True, fontsize=10, title_fontsize=11, borderpad=1, labelspacing=1)
legend.get_frame().set_edgecolor('#e0e0e0')
legend.get_frame().set_facecolor('white')

# Set axes labels and title
ax.set_xlabel('Education Spending (% of GDP)', fontsize=12, labelpad=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Average PISA Score (2022)', fontsize=12, labelpad=12, fontweight='bold')

plt.suptitle('Education Investment vs. Outcomes: A Global Perspective', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=0.96, x=0.05, ha='left', color='#222222')
ax.set_title('Higher spending does not strictly guarantee better test scores or youth labor outcomes.\nSize represents tertiary enrollment; color represents youth unemployment.', fontsize=12, color='#555555', loc='left', pad=15)

# Add notable labels
notable_countries = ['Singapore', 'South Korea', 'Japan', 'Estonia', 'Finland', 'Sweden', 
                     'United States', 'Costa Rica', 'Brazil', 'Spain', 'Greece', 'Ireland', 'Italy', 'Australia']

# Try to avoid label overlap using adjustText if installed, else manual offsets
texts = []
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    if row['country'] in notable_countries:
        ax.annotate(row['country'], 
                    (row['edu_spending_pct_gdp'], row['pisa_avg']),
                    xytext=(5, 5), textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')

# Fine-tune grid and axes limits
ax.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

# Spines
for spine in ['top', 'right']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)

# Add source note
plt.figtext(0.05, 0.02, 'Source: World Bank, OECD Estimates (circa 2022-2023). Based on 30 selected countries.', fontsize=9, color='#777777', ha='left')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.05, 1, 0.93])

# Save
import os
os.makedirs('/app/output', exist_ok=True)
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > plot.py
import json
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np
from adjustText import adjust_text

# Read data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Extract lists
df_spend = pd.DataFrame(data['education_spending']['data'])
df_pisa = pd.DataFrame(data['pisa_scores']['data'])
df_enroll = pd.DataFrame(data['tertiary_enrollment']['data'])
df_unemp = pd.DataFrame(data['youth_unemployment']['data'])

# Merge
df = df_spend.merge(df_pisa, on='country')
df = df.merge(df_enroll, on='country')
df = df.merge(df_unemp, on='country')

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'sans-serif'
plt.rcParams['font.sans-serif'] = ['Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans']
plt.rcParams['axes.edgecolor'] = '#555555'
plt.rcParams['axes.linewidth'] = 1.0
plt.rcParams['axes.labelcolor'] = '#333333'
plt.rcParams['xtick.color'] = '#333333'
plt.rcParams['ytick.color'] = '#333333'

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(15, 9.5))

# Create scatter plot
scatter = ax.scatter(
    df['edu_spending_pct_gdp'], 
    df['pisa_avg'], 
    s=df['enrollment_rate'] * 12, # scale up size
    c=df['youth_unemp_rate'], 
    cmap='viridis_r', # reverse viridis: low unemp (good) is yellow/green, high unemp (bad) is dark purple
    alpha=0.8, 
    edgecolors='#ffffff', 
    linewidth=1.2
)

# Add colorbar for youth unemployment
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax, shrink=0.6, aspect=15, pad=0.03)
cbar.set_label('Youth Unemployment Rate (%)', fontsize=12, labelpad=12, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=10, colors='#333333')
cbar.outline.set_visible(False)

# Add size legend for enrollment
sizes = [50, 75, 100]
legend_elements = [plt.scatter([], [], s=size*12, c='#cccccc', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='white', label=f'{size}%') for size in sizes]
legend = ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, title='Tertiary Enrollment\n(% of age cohort)', loc='lower right', 
                   frameon=True, fontsize=11, title_fontsize=12, borderpad=1.2, labelspacing=1.5, edgecolor='#dddddd')
legend.get_frame().set_facecolor('#ffffff')
legend.get_frame().set_alpha(0.9)

# Set axes labels and title
ax.set_xlabel('Education Spending (% of GDP)', fontsize=13, labelpad=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Average PISA Score (2022)', fontsize=13, labelpad=12, fontweight='bold')

plt.suptitle('The Education Investment Paradox: Spending vs. Outcomes', fontsize=22, fontweight='bold', y=0.97, x=0.04, ha='left', color='#111111')
ax.set_title('Higher spending does not consistently correlate with better PISA scores or labor market integration.\nCircle size represents university enrollment rate; color indicates youth unemployment rate.', fontsize=13, color='#444444', loc='left', pad=15, linespacing=1.5)

# Add notable labels
notable_countries = [
    'Singapore', 'South Korea', 'Japan', 'Estonia', 'Finland', 'Sweden', 
    'United States', 'Costa Rica', 'Brazil', 'Spain', 'Greece', 'Ireland', 
    'Italy', 'Australia', 'Chile', 'Turkey', 'France', 'Germany', 'Norway'
]

# Create texts for adjustText
texts = []
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    if row['country'] in notable_countries:
        texts.append(ax.text(row['edu_spending_pct_gdp'], row['pisa_avg'], row['country'], 
                             fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', color='#222222'))

# Adjust text to prevent overlap
adjust_text(texts, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color='#888888', lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
            expand_points=(1.5, 1.5), force_points=(0.5, 0.5))

# Fine-tune grid and axes limits
ax.grid(True, linestyle=':', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

# Remove top and right spines
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Expand limits slightly to fit bubbles and labels
x_min, x_max = df['edu_spending_pct_gdp'].min(), df['edu_spending_pct_gdp'].max()
y_min, y_max = df['pisa_avg'].min(), df['pisa_avg'].max()
ax.set_xlim(x_min - 0.5, x_max + 0.5)
ax.set_ylim(y_min - 20, y_max + 20)

# Add quadrant/highlight annotations if desired, or keep it clean.
# Let's add a couple of subtle analytical annotations as requested by the "editorial, layered" style.

ax.text(3.1, 555, 'High Efficiency\n(High PISA, Low Spend)', fontsize=11, color='#0066cc', style='italic', alpha=0.8, bbox=dict(facecolor='white', alpha=0.6, edgecolor='none', pad=2))
ax.text(6.3, 385, 'Divergent Outcomes\n(High Spend, Low PISA)', fontsize=11, color='#cc4400', style='italic', alpha=0.8, bbox=dict(facecolor='white', alpha=0.6, edgecolor='none', pad=2))

# Add source note
plt.figtext(0.04, 0.02, 'Source: World Bank, OECD Estimates (circa 2022). Analysis covers 30 selected countries.', fontsize=10, color='#666666', ha='left')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.04, 1, 0.92])

# Save
import os
os.makedirs('/app/output', exist_ok=True)
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
EOF
python3 plot.py
